questions.q: What does the approx_kl metric measure during PPO training?
options: The total reward collected in the last episode
An estimate of how much the policy actually changed between the old and new policy after an update
The size of the replay buffer
The number of parallel environments in use
questions.explain: approx_kl is the practical echo of TRPO's trust region, measuring the average KL-divergence between the old and new policy after each update.

questions.q: What does it mean if clip_fraction is consistently near 1 throughout training?
options: Training is healthy and proceeding normally
Almost every sample's probability ratio is being clipped, suggesting updates are trying to move the policy much further than the trust region allows
The critic has stopped learning
The environment has no reward signal
questions.explain: A clip_fraction near 1 means nearly all samples hit the clipping boundary, indicating the policy update is attempting much larger changes than the clip range permits — often a sign the learning rate or clip_range needs adjustment.

questions.q: What does a low or negative explained_variance indicate?
options: The policy has too much entropy
The critic's value predictions are not explaining the actual observed returns well — it isn't learning a useful value function
The clip_range is set too conservatively
The replay buffer is empty
questions.explain: explained_variance near 0 or negative means the critic's predictions are no better (or worse) than just predicting the mean return, signaling a critic that isn't learning properly.

questions.q: What is a likely cause of entropy crashing to near-zero very early in PPO training?
options: The learning rate is too small
The policy has collapsed to near-deterministic behavior before sufficient exploration, often requiring a higher entropy bonus coefficient
The critic's value function is too accurate
The replay buffer capacity is too large
questions.explain: A sharp early entropy drop signals premature convergence to deterministic behavior; increasing the entropy bonus coefficient c2 is a common fix.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where do most real-world PPO failures actually originate?
options: Bugs in the clipped surrogate objective formula itself
Bugs in the advantage estimate (e.g. GAE sign errors, off-by-one issues) or hyperparameters mismatched to the problem, rather than the clipped objective itself
The environment's reward function always being wrong
PyTorch's automatic differentiation engine
questions.explain: The clipped objective is a short, well-tested formula; most practical failures trace back to bugs in advantage computation (like GAE wiring) or hyperparameters like learning rate and clip_range that don't suit the problem.
